advice: Propose an experimental 32-row A-tile transpose-and-consume pipeline using the existing NN full512 kernel as the comparison. For each packed 64-row band and each 64-column B panel, keep B packing and the current output blocks unchanged. For the first and second 32-row halves, transpose the needed A rows in small K-by-row tiles into a bounded temporary tile, then feed those values directly to the existing FP32 FMOPA loop instead of writing the full 128 KiB packed-A scratch. Map A[i,k] into the same packed vectors currently read by the K loop, preserving each output tile's K order. The fused path must cover each input element needed by both consumers exactly once; it must not recompute the transpose for separate column panels. This tests whether removing full-scratch writes and reads offsets the added tile handling. Expected effect is unknown and must be measured.
risks: The proposal is not yet an implementation recipe: the supplied evidence does not specify a legal SME instruction sequence for retaining a transposed tile and supplying its values to FMOPA, nor establish that tile storage avoids extra copies. A naïve per-column-panel transpose repeats A conversion 16 times, adding up to 15 extra reads/conversions per needed A tile; reject that variant unless its complete repeated work is deliberately the experiment. A fused design may also increase register pressure, ZA transfers, loop overhead, or stack use, and may change rounding if it changes each accumulator's K order. Do not assume scratch traffic is the bottleneck. Keep FP32 accumulation order, ABI, thread count, tolerance, fallback and licenses unchanged; allocate all temporary storage inside gemm, handle allocation failure with the original NN path, preserve fresh inputs, and fully overwrite C. First check the exact operand-to-tile mapping and bounds for all 512 K values and both row halves; then validate n=512 plus general sizes, odd tails and n<=0. If a legal instruction-level design cannot preserve K order and avoid repeated transpose work, abstain rather than inventing one. If implemented, use ten validation reports and ten fresh alternating paired controls with the frozen best-of-three report rule, unchanged power settings, the 1.05 separated-ranges gate and held-out check; report both historical and fresh same-mode peak comparisons. No measured effect is established.
